title: Colnago Y1Rs Review - The Best Aero Road Bike?

takeaways.text: The cantilevered seat mast must be cut to length; the effective seat angle is conventional, and the gull-wing cockpit offers no usable tops position for long climbs.
Bike-only it saved 37.1 W against Cyclingnews' baseline (the fastest bike saved 40.3 W); with a rider it was top five, 3.7 W behind the Cervélo S5, and it gains in crosswinds.
Livelier and more race-geometry than older Colnagos, fast-feeling and stiff at the rear, but vertically harsh and less precise than a Dogma.
The tester felt the narrow bayonet-fork junction and tall front triangle made the front end twist under braking and sprinting, and he experienced a speed wobble.
The top build was US$21,000 without a power meter or top-tier tires, and the Di2 cable needed electrical tape because no grommet was supplied.

disclosure: Publication review with Cyclingnews wind-tunnel testing; the complete Dura-Ace build tested differs from the candidate's mainland frame kit.
summary: Cyclingnews' ride and wind-tunnel review of the Colnago Y1Rs aero race bike in a size 56.
